display.title: Episode 135: Rabbi Akiva in Prison and The Drunken Father (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: Joining Tzivos Hashem to beat the Yetzer Hara, why water purifies, Rabbi Akiva washing negel vasser in prison, Ahavas Yisroel, and a sad story about a father who drinks.
display.summary_long: A Three Weeks program. Uncle Yossi invites children to join Tzivos Hashem and receive an ID card, emblem and wallet, and explains that Torah and mitzvos are the secret weapons that will make the Yetzer Hara surrender before Moshiach comes. A girl from a Boro Park school leads the Shema. Then he describes Hashem's gift of water, which gives life, keeps us healthy and also makes us pure, like the Kohanim washing at the Mishkan, which is why we wash negel vasser each morning. In the story, Rabbi Akiva is jailed for teaching Torah and given no water for three days; when a jug finally comes he uses it to wash his hands with a brachah, and the amazed ruler frees him and makes him an adviser. Uncle Yossi teaches Rabbi Akiva's great rule, love your fellow as yourself, and the Alter Rebbe's teaching that loving every Jew leads to loving Hashem, so important in the Three Weeks. He ends with a story 'with no happy ending': young Naftali shows his drinking father a drunkard in the street, but the father only asks where to get such a good drink. The Torah shows us the ways of other nations only so we will not copy them.
display.lesson: Torah and mitzvos are our weapons against the Yetzer Hara; love every Jew as yourself; and learn from others' bad ways only to avoid them.

date.note: 'Especially today during the Three Weeks'; between 134 (24 Tammuz, Rosh Chodesh Av next Monday) and 136 (Tisha B'Av program).

advisories.note: Rabbi Akiva is jailed for teaching Torah and given no water for three days.
A boy is ashamed of his father's drinking; a drunk lies in the street.
The drunken father story deliberately ends without the father changing.

privacy.note: Shema guest named in full with her school.

sources_cited.note: 'V'ahavta l'reiacha kamocha'; Rabbi Akiva calls it a great rule of the Torah, 'as written in the Gemara'.
The Alter Rebbe: Ahavas Yisroel leads to Ahavas Hashem.
'Like the practice of the land of Egypt... you shall not do' (Parshas Acharei).
